title: The Last Day of Summer
author: ReadingPlanet Staff
summary: Marcus faces the end of summer and must say goodbye to his best friend who is moving away.

vocabulary.definition: a feeling that is both happy and sad at the same time
vocabulary.sentence: Saying goodbye to his friend was bittersweet for Marcus.

vocabulary.definition: in a way that shows unwillingness or hesitation
vocabulary.sentence: Marcus reluctantly packed up his things, not wanting the day to end.

vocabulary.definition: the line where the earth or sea seems to meet the sky
vocabulary.sentence: The sun slowly sank toward the horizon.

content.text: Marcus sat on the dock, his feet dangling over the still lake water. Tomorrow, everything would change. School would start. His best friend Damon would be gone. The summer of endless bike rides, video game marathons, and late-night conversations would become just a memory.
"You're thinking too much again," Damon said, dropping down beside him. "I can tell by your face."
"I'm not thinking. I'm just... looking at the water."

Damon laughed. "Sure. And I'm not about to move 800 miles away tomorrow." He picked up a stone and skipped it across the glassy surface. Four skips before it sank. "Remember when you couldn't skip rocks at all?"
Marcus smiled despite himself. "You hit me in the head with one. Three times."
"It was twice, and you moved into the path." Damon found another flat stone. "Here. Your turn."
Marcus took the stone. It was smooth and warm from sitting in the sun. He flicked his wrist the way Damon had taught him years ago. The stone bounced five times across the water. A new personal best.
"See?" Damon said. "You'll be fine without me."
"That's not—" Marcus started, then stopped. They both knew that wasn't the point.

The sun was sinking toward the horizon now, painting the sky in shades of orange and pink. They had watched countless sunsets from this dock over the years. This would be their last one together for a long time.
"You know we can video chat," Damon said quietly. "And there's winter break. My mom already said you could visit."
"Yeah." Marcus's voice came out rough. "It won't be the same though."
"No," Damon agreed. "But maybe that's okay. Different doesn't have to mean worse." He paused. "My dad says change is just life's way of making room for new adventures."

Marcus wasn't sure he believed that. But sitting here next to his best friend, watching the sun melt into the water, he could almost imagine it might be true. Tomorrow would bring a new school year, new challenges, and the empty space where Damon used to be. But it would also bring possibilities he couldn't see yet.
"Race you back to the house?" Damon asked, already getting to his feet.
Marcus stood up slowly, taking one last look at the darkening water. "You always cheat."
"I call it strategic advantage." Damon grinned. "Ready?"
Marcus nodded. Whatever tomorrow brought, he would face it. But tonight, he still had his best friend, a summer sunset, and one last race to run.
